sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious and on a ventilator following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence, alleging prison officials botched the lethal injection. They state officials used at least seven needles, bending one, while Pike whimpered and cried. An expert suggested the drug pentobarbital entered tissue under her skin rather than her bloodstream due to ruptured veins or blood clots.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in the state for the year and ordered an independent review. Pike's lawyers had previously warned that her blood-clotting condition and small veins risked causing unnecessary pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities have not yet said whether they will attempt to execute Pike again, and her lawyers are seeking to preserve all physical, written, and electronic evidence.

sections.text: At Oktoberfest in Munich, the operator of the Teufelsrad ride has been giving free cycling shorts to women and girls in dresses to protect them from upskirting. sections.text: Author Min Jin Lee is publishing her third novel, American Hagwon, which explores the Korean diaspora and the intense culture of private cram schools. sections.text: Polish campaigners launched a 22-compartment pink parcel locker called the AbortOmat in Warsaw to allow women to access abortion pills anonymously using a six-digit code. The locker is located inside an abortion centre opened by the Abortion Dream Team.

sections.text: Providing abortion medication or helping someone obtain it is a crime in Poland punishable by up to three years in prison. The locker challenges these strict restrictions by using a machine as an intermediary to make legality more vague.

timeline.text: Do humans really have a ‘lizard brain’ lurking beneath our rational minds?

gist: Paul D MacLean proposed the triune brain model in 1959.
The triune model suggests humans have a lizard, mammalian, and rational brain.
Neurobiologists now consider the triune brain model deeply misleading and inaccurate.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In 1959, Paul D MacLean proposed the triune brain model, suggesting humans possess three layered brains: a primitive lizard brain, a mammalian emotional brain, and a rational neomammalian cortex. This idea became extremely popular.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Neurobiologists now consider the onion-like brain analogy deeply misleading. Evolution does not add neatly divisible mental capacities. Modern anatomical and behavioural evidence shows reptiles possess mammalian features and lower animals solve complex problems.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Despite being discredited by evolutionary and physiological evidence, the triune brain concept endures and is still widely taught in introductory psychology textbooks.

fivew: The triune brain model proposing three layered brains in humans was debunked.
Evolutionary and physiological evidence shows the brain is a dynamic, integrated system rather than separate layers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The curriculum and assessment review published in November 2025 recommended clarifying what counts as statutory and non-statutory content before a new national curriculum is due next spring. The government promised to strengthen history teaching and let teachers reflect Black history. sections.text: Enslavement is deeply embedded in British society, influencing the economy, ports, and empire. When the topic remains optional, teachers often skip it due to curriculum overload, leaving critical gaps in students' understanding of British history.

gist: Portable MP3 players revolutionized music consumption in the 2000s before smartphones and streaming took over.
Vintage iPods and modded devices are seeing a resurgence alongside new retro-focused hardware startups.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Portable digital music began in 1998 with early devices like the MPMan F10 and Diamond Rio PMP300. Apple dominated the 2000s with the iPod, capturing over 70 percent of sales. By 2012, smartphones and streaming caused the industry to collapse from $21.6 billion to $613 million.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: A growing anti-streaming sentiment and slowtech trend have sparked renewed interest in offline listening. Vintage iPods fetch high prices on eBay, spawning a modding industry and cheap knockoffs from overseas manufacturers.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: As working used units eventually run out, startups like Sleevenote are attempting fresh concepts. However, a full resurgence on the scale of vinyl remains unlikely due to a lack of collectibility.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ben Lidgey discovered he had testicular cancer after his four-year-old son accidentally kicked him while playing in the garden. He initially delayed seeking medical help, thinking the pain would pass. Following his treatment, he later received counselling for post-cancer challenges. Meanwhile, the charity Movember published a report highlighting high rates of premature death among men in Wales.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Men in Wales face higher rates of premature death compared to women, often from preventable conditions or suicide. Experts cite a reluctance to seek medical and mental health support, traditional expectations of masculinity, and deprivation as key factors contributing to poorer health outcomes.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Movember is calling on the Welsh government to develop a dedicated men's health plan. The government stated that its existing strategies on suicide prevention, self-harm, mental health, and cancer are already working to address these challenges.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Michigan state police clarified that convicted abuser Larry Nassar was never removed from the state sex offender registry. An Eaton county prosecutor's office incorrectly asserted he was removed following a supreme court decision on older offenses. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The supreme court ruled the state's sex offender registration law cannot be applied retroactively, leading to the removal of over 20,000 entries. Experts warn that children's books lack incidental representation where identity does not drive plots.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A study by Inclusive Books for Children revealed a decline in diverse main characters in UK books for under-10s in 2025. Books with Black main characters fell by 7.8%, while south Asian representation dropped to 1.4%. Books featuring Middle Eastern and North African characters halved to just three, all of which focused on refugee experiences. Disabled main characters in picture books also fell by 60%.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts argue children need stories reflecting their lives to encourage reading. They highlighted a lack of "incidental representation", where diverse characters star in ordinary stories rather than having their identity drive the plot.

gist: A holiday cottage company demanded a death certificate to amend a booking after a bereavement.
The family faced distressing bureaucratic hurdles and automated emails asking if the deceased enjoyed the stay.
A consumer champion intervened, securing a full refund and a goodwill payment from the company.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A customer died before a family holiday booked with Sykes Holiday Cottages. The company refused to transfer the booking name without formal proof of death, rejecting a marriage certificate, an inquest listing, and a GP letter, while repeatedly emailing the deceased customer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The company lacked an official bereavement policy and showed a severe lack of empathy during a vulnerable time, imposing onerous requirements for a simple name change.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Following intervention, the company refunded the £2,400 cost plus £150 in goodwill, apologized directly to the family, and stated it is reviewing its processes.

fivew: Sykes Holiday Cottages and a bereaved family.

Harry Kane scored twice before being rested, with Bellingham taking the armband.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England defeated Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka during the Nations League. Jude Bellingham scored and provided three assists, later wearing the captain's armband after Harry Kane was rested. Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each scored twice, while Anthony Gordon also scored and assisted.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The performance highlighted Bellingham's growing leadership and world-class potential, with pundits suggesting he could become one of football's greatest players. Thomas Tuchel noted that Bellingham has unlocked a new level of performance after taking on additional responsibility following the World Cup.

gist: Scotland defeated North Macedonia two nil in a dominant Nations League match.
Kieron Bowie and John McGinn scored for Scotland in the comfortable victory.
Andy Robertson earned his 100th cap during the straightforward away win.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scotland dominated North Macedonia with twenty five shots to nine, securing a two nil win. Kieron Bowie scored an early goal, and John McGinn added a second from a penalty after Scott McKenna was sent off late in the game.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory lifted pressure off head coach Sebastien Pocognoli and provided a morale boost. Andy Robertson celebrated his 100th cap, while younger players gained valuable experience in a dominant team performance.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Scotland prepares to face Slovenia at Hampden on Tuesday in their final game of the current series.

timeline.text: Leicester hold off Newcastle for first Prem win

gist: Leicester Tigers defeated Newcastle Red Bulls to secure their first win of the season.
Former Newcastle winger Adam Radwan scored against his old club during the match.
Newcastle mounted a late comeback effort but ultimately fell short at home.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Leicester Tigers won their first match of the season with a hard-fought victory away against Newcastle Red Bulls. Tries from Samiuela Moli, Adam Radwan and Will Hurd helped Leicester establish a lead, while Billy Searle contributed with conversions and a penalty. Newcastle responded with scores from Obi Ene, George McGuigan and Cameron Jordan, alongside kicks from Brett Connon and Zack Henry, but Leicester held on to win.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory marked Leicester's first win in seven matches across all competitions, ending a poor run of form stretching back into the previous season. For Newcastle, the defeat came in their first home match of the campaign despite a positive showing and a late comeback attempt.
